newsitem.title: USA: Unocal to increase U.S Gulf oil drilling.
newsitem.headline: Unocal to increase U.S Gulf oil drilling.

text.p: Unocal Corp will increase deepwater oil drilling in the U.S. Gulf starting in 1998 as part of plan to rebuild reserves, the company said Friday.

The company's domestic exploration and production division, Spirit Energy 76, plans to drill 46 deepwater wells by the end of 1998, and about 30 exploration wells per year on the outer continental shelf through 2001.
Unocal Corp will increase capital investment sharply from 1998 through 2001, averaging almost $500 million annually, the company said.
That would represent an increase from an expected $330 million this year, the company said earlier.
"Our growth is focused on a deepwater campaign targeted at adding 400 million barrels of oil equivalent (mmboe) in reserves by 2002," said Jack Schanck, president of Spirit Energy 76.
Current industry estimates are that 15-30 billion barrels of oil equivalent remain in undiscovered deepwater prospects, the company said.
Onshore, Spirit Energy 76 plans to expand its use of 3-D surveys to drill seven to 10 wells annually, targeting annual increases in reserves of 10 mmboe.
The company expects to reduce finding and development costs from over $10 per barrel of oil equivalent over the last three years to as little as $5, as reserves from deepwater discoveries are added.

Spirit Energy 76 is the third largest producer in the U.S. Gulf of Mexico, with 300 platforms and 2,700 active wells in 355 fields. In 1996, it produced an average of 912 million cubic feet of natural gas and about 52,000 barrels of oil per day.
